title: t-SNI-R Security of SecMultILR2
summary: SecMultILR2 has a known but complex t-SNI proof, while its strengthened t-SNI-R security remains unresolved; prove the property or give a counterexample.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the $\mathrm{SecMultILR2}$ multiplication gadget satisfies $\mathrm{t\text{-}SNI\text{-}R}$, the strengthened probing-security property that permits an adversary to obtain a designated subset of gadget randomness with a single probe. A $\mathrm{t\text{-}SNI}$ security proof for $\mathrm{SecMultILR2}$ is known but is already complex, and its $\mathrm{t\text{-}SNI\text{-}R}$ security was left unproved. Prove that $\mathrm{SecMultILR2}$ satisfies $\mathrm{t\text{-}SNI\text{-}R}$, or give a counterexample.

scope.domain: Side-channel cryptanalysis of masked multiplication gadgets and probing-security properties.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether SecMultILR2 satisfies t-SNI-R; the task is to prove the property or give a counterexample.

progress.summary: The source says the existing t-SNI security proof for SecMultILR2 is already complex and therefore does not attempt to prove t-SNI-R. It consequently uses the multiple-PRG approach only for SecMultFLR and SecMultILR.
citation_labels: Jean-Sébastien Coron et al., Side-channel Masking with Pseudo-Random Generator
